entry.title: docs(analysis): Document the CloudWatch metricDataQueries fields (#5194)
entry.content:
docs(analysis): Document the CloudWatch metricDataQueries fields (#5194)

* docs(analysis): Document the CloudWatch metricDataQueries fields

The CloudWatch page only linked to the AWS MetricDataQuery API and its
example never used dimensions or label, although both are part of the
provider's schema (CloudWatchMetricDataQuery / CloudWatchMetricStatMetric
in analysis_types.go). Add a field table and show a dimension in the
example.

Signed-off-by: Bhavishya Jain <65864699+bhavishyajain545@users.noreply.github.com>

* docs(analysis): Give both CloudWatch queries the same Service dimension

CloudWatch treats a metric with and without a dimension as different
series, so the errors/requests rate in the example compared the
service's errors against the undimensioned requests metric.

Signed-off-by: Bhavishya Jain <65864699+bhavishyajain545@users.noreply.github.com>

* docs(analysis): Add a Required column to the CloudWatch field table

Same layout as the Kayenta page. Requirements follow the CloudWatch
GetMetricData API: id, one of expression or metricStat, and for
metricStat the metric namespace and name, period and stat.

Signed-off-by: Bhavishya Jain <65864699+bhavishyajain545@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Signed-off-by: Bhavishya Jain <65864699+bhavishyajain545@users.noreply.github.com>

entry.title: docs(analysis): Fix the Kayenta examples and document all provider fi…
entry.content:
docs(analysis): Fix the Kayenta examples and document all provider fields (#5193)

* docs(analysis): Fix the Kayenta examples and document all provider fields

The Kayenta examples did not match the API: the field is threshold, not
thresholds; metricsAccountName, configurationAccountName and
storageAccountName are required by the CRD but were missing; region is
required in every scope; and interval/count were shown under the provider
although they are metric-level fields. Fix the examples and add a field
table.

Signed-off-by: Bhavishya Jain <65864699+bhavishyajain545@users.noreply.github.com>

* docs(analysis): Explain which account the canary config lookup uses

getCanaryConfigId builds the lookup URL with storageAccountName as the
configurationAccountName query parameter, so the examples now use one
account for config and storage and the field table says so.

Signed-off-by: Bhavishya Jain <65864699+bhavishyajain545@users.noreply.github.com>

entry.title: fix: avoid int32 overflow when maxTrafficWeight is large (#4923)
entry.content:
fix: avoid int32 overflow when maxTrafficWeight is large (#4923)

replicas and weights were multiplied as int32 before being widened, so
a large maxTrafficWeight overflowed the product and the canary counts
came out wrong. With maxTrafficWeight=100000000, a 43 replica rollout at
50% weight produced -21 canary replicas, and at 100% weight it produced
1 canary replica instead of 43.

Widen the operands before multiplying, the way trafficWeightToReplicas
already does.

Signed-off-by: semx <7532921+semx@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: semx <7532921+semx@users.noreply.github.com>
